evidence.section: Failure Modes at RT and 500 oC
evidence.quote: It can be inferred that at RT fatigue cracks initiated and propagated as follows: Fatigue cracks first initiated from surface or subsurface defects due to the high stress intensity factor, and then propagated from the edge quickly in the brittle coating, next crossed the interface without the delamination along the interface, and finally gathered into the center.

evidence.quote: the longer fatigue life at 500 oC is mainly because of the relatively lower interface strength at high temperature, resulting in the time-consuming process of dimple formation in both the coating and substrate.
at room temperature (RT), the fatigue strength of specimens welded by the acetylene gas welding (AGW) was lower than that of specimens welded by the plasma transferred arc welding (PTAW).
For PTAW specimens, the fatigue strength at 500 oC was much higher than that at RT.
